answer: Admission needs a live-ice stake survey. The applicant locks 37 coins and completes a 6.4 km packed voyage along a published glacier centerline, driving a clerk-serialized juniper wand into ablation marker 14 whose weekly melt table is on-ledger. In 28 minutes they pour a 40 ml fluorescein pulse and file a 90-second film of the wand, dye front, and marker plate. Peers require GPS within 8 m, dye arrival within 2.1 min of the melt table, and the wand serial in every frame. A studio tray or borrowed wand misses both checks and burns the stake, so each alias needs its own walk, wand, and ice.
